name: gridcraft-edge-mcp

tools.name: sheet_create
tools.description: Make a well-formatted .xlsx in one call and attach it for download. Never write Python or other code to create, read or edit spreadsheets. Each sheet has columns and rows; headers are bold, frozen and filtered by default. Numbers/booleans are JSON primitives; dates are ISO YYYY-MM-DD with kind:date; formulas use {formula:"=SUM(B2:B5)"}. Plain strings remain text. Limits: 16 sheets, 10000 data rows per sheet, 128 columns, 100000 total cells including headers; dropped items are reported in warnings. Path defaults to Spreadsheet.xlsx under --root; existing names get a suffix and are never replaced.

number_format.description: Optional Excel number format code (max 256 bytes)

tools.name: file_attach
tools.description: Return an existing file under --root as an embedded resource the user can download. Read-only, regular files up to 32 MiB. Supports xlsx, csv, pdf, docx and pptx; use .xlsx for downloadable spreadsheets in LibreChat (CSV is model text). Call after saving edits.

path.description: Relative or absolute file path inside --root

tools.name: execute_command
tools.description: Run ANY GridCraft command by id with JSON params — every ribbon/menu action is a command. Find ids and parameter docs with list_commands. Examples: {"command":"cell.set","params":{"cell":"B2","input":"=SUM(A1:A9)"}}; {"command":"home.bold","params":{"range":"A1:C1"}}; {"command":"sheet.insert"}; {"command":"data.removeDuplicates","params":{"range":"A1:C20"}}. Most commands act on the current selection when `range` is omitted. Programmatic calls never open dialogs: missing required params give an error.

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

params.description: Command parameters (see the `params` field of list_commands); omit or {} for defaults

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: list_windows
tools.description: List the open windows: window id, workbook (`doc`) id, title ("Book1", or "Book1:2" for a workbook's second window), unsaved changes, active and hidden. Pass a `window` or `doc` id to other tools to act there.

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: List GridCraft commands: id, label, ribbon path, shortcut, a parameter description (`params`) and whether it can run right now. Use it to discover what execute_command can do (e.g. search "sort", "border", "chart", "sheet").

search.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against id, label and ribbon path

tools.name: inspect_workbook
tools.description: Summary of the active workbook: title, path, dirty flag, sheets (name, used range, cell count, tables, charts, merges, filters, freeze panes), defined names, current selection and active cell, calculation mode and undo/redo history.

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: read_range
tools.description: Read cell values from a range as rows (2-D array). Numbers/booleans/strings are returned as JSON values, empty cells as null, errors as {"error":"#DIV/0!"}. Without `range`, reads the sheet's used range. formulas:true returns formula text ("=SUM(B2:B4)") for formula cells; formatted:true returns the displayed text ("$1,234.00", "12%").

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

formatted.description: Return display text with number formats applied

formulas.description: Return formulas instead of computed values for formula cells

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: write_range
tools.description: Write a 2-D array of values starting at the top-left cell of `range` (rows of cells). Numbers, booleans, null (clears) and strings are accepted; strings starting with = are formulas ("=SUM(B2:B4)"), other strings are parsed like typed input ("12%", "1/2/2024", "$5") unless `parse` is false, which stores them as the text they are. The result's `converted` lists the strings that were read as something else. One undo step. Example: {"range":"A1","values":[["Item","Cost"],["Rent",1200]]}.

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

parse.description: Read strings not starting with = like typed input, so "05.04.2026" becomes a date (default true); false stores them as the text they are, and "" clears the cell

range.description: Top-left cell or range, e.g. "A1" or "Sheet2!B3"

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: set_cell
tools.description: Enter one cell exactly as if typed: a number, text, or a formula starting with = ("=AVERAGE(B2:B9)"). Dependent cells recalculate. Returns the command result; use get_cell to read the computed value.

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: get_cell
tools.description: Details of one cell: computed value and type, formula, display text, raw input, spill range, style, merge, comment and hyperlink.

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: evaluate_formula
tools.description: Evaluate a formula against the active sheet WITHOUT changing any cell, e.g. "=SUM(B2:B10)/COUNT(B2:B10)" or "=VLOOKUP(\"x\",A:B,2,FALSE)". `cell` sets the formula's position for relative references and ROW()/COLUMN(). Use English function names and `,` between arguments; a formula that couldn't be entered in a cell is an error saying why.

cell.description: Evaluate as if in this cell (default: active cell)

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

formula.description: Formula text, with or without the leading =

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: select
tools.description: Set the selection (what commands without a `range` param act on). Multiple areas with commas: "A1:B2,D4". A "Sheet2!A1" prefix switches sheets.

active.description: Active cell inside the selection (default: top-left of the last area)

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: format_range
tools.description: Apply several formats to a range in one call: bold, italic, underline, font name/size, font color, fill color, number format, horizontal alignment, wrap, borders. Colors are "#RRGGBB" (fontColor also "auto", fillColor also "none"). numberFormat is a name (General, Number, Currency, Accounting, Comma, Percentage, Short Date, Long Date, Time, Fraction, Scientific, Text) or a format code ("#,##0.00", "0%", "yyyy-mm-dd"). Each property runs one command; the result lists them.

borders.description: A border preset name, or {preset, style?, color?}

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: insert_chart
tools.description: Insert a chart from a data range (first row/column used as series names and categories, like Excel). Returns the chart id.

at.description: Top-left anchor cell (default: right of the data)

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

range.description: Source data range including headers, e.g. "A1:C6"

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: create_table
tools.description: Format a range as an Excel table (structured references, banded rows, filter buttons). The first row is the header by default.

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

range.description: Range including the header row, e.g. "A1:D20"

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: sort_range
tools.description: Sort a range by one or more columns. keys: [{"column":"B","order":"desc"}, …] or just ["B"]. Without `range` the current region around the selection is sorted; header detection follows Excel unless `header` is given.

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

header.description: The first row is a header (kept in place)

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: filter
tools.description: Filter rows by a column (turns on AutoFilter on the current region, or `range`, when needed). Give `values` (keep rows whose cell text is one of them), `custom` ({op:">", value:"10", op2?, value2?, and?}), `top` ({count, bottom?, percent?}), or clear:true to remove this column's filter.

custom.description: Custom criteria: {op: "="|"<>"|">"|">="|"<"|"<="|"beginsWith"|"contains"…, value, op2?, value2?, and?: bool}

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

range.description: Data range to filter (default: the current region of the selection)

top.description: Top/bottom N: {count, bottom?: bool, percent?: bool}

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: open_workbook
tools.description: Open the user's attached spreadsheet using the exact absolute upload path provided in context (or a relative path inside --root). Never write Python or other code to create, read or edit a spreadsheet. Edit with GridCraft, save_workbook under a new .xlsx name, then file_attach the returned path for download. Supports xlsx, xlsm, xls, xlsb, ods, csv, tsv, txt, json; check import warnings for unsupported features.

tools.name: save_workbook
tools.description: Save the active workbook. The format follows the extension (.xlsx default; .csv/.tsv save the active sheet; .json; .html). With --root, saves as a new unused .xlsx name (including when path is omitted), preserving the upload. Call file_attach with the returned path for download. Without --root, omitted path saves to the current file.

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: new_workbook
tools.description: Create a new workbook and make it active: blank, or a built-in sample ("budget", "sales", "grades").

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last change(s) to the active workbook.

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone change(s).

doc.description: Workbook id from list_windows: its most recent window (default: the active window)

window.description: Window id from list_windows (default: the active window)

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Save a PNG screenshot of the GridCraft window to `path`. Desktop app only (`gridcraft-cli mcp --connect 7979`).

tools.name: list_functions
tools.description: List worksheet functions: name, category, signature and description. Filter with `search` (name or description) or `category`.

search.description: Substring of the name or description

instructions: GridCraft makes and edits spreadsheets. To make a new spreadsheet, call sheet_create: it saves a formatted .xlsx and attaches it for download in one call. When the user attaches a spreadsheet, its absolute path is given in context: open that exact path with open_workbook, edit it, save_workbook under a new .xlsx name, then call file_attach so the user can download it. Never write Python or other code to create, read or edit a spreadsheet. To give the user any file a tool wrote, call file_attach with its path. Check import warnings: features GridCraft does not model may not survive saving. Cells use A1 notation ("B2", "A1:D10", "Sheet2!A1:B3"). Every action is a command: find ids and parameters with list_commands and run any of them with execute_command. Convenience tools cover the common flow: write_range / set_cell to enter values and formulas (strings starting with = are formulas), read_range / get_cell to read computed values back, format_range, create_table, insert_chart, sort_range, filter, evaluate_formula (try a formula without changing the sheet), undo / redo, open_workbook / save_workbook. inspect_workbook summarizes sheets, used ranges, tables, charts and names. list_functions lists the worksheet functions.  Backend: headless (in-process engine, no window).
